# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4645

# Review — PAN-4645
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — the desktop-packaged server cannot load `@hyperswarm/secret-stream`, and a revoked `/ws/rpc` client keeps running RPCs for up to 30 s

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4645-review-9f37570f
- Manifest: .pan/review/agent-pan-4645-review-9f37570f/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4645 / workspaces/feature-pan-4645 (PR #4715)
- HEAD reviewed: 9f37570fc141f7c9e8230023a9b461fd2b013d3e
- Base / prior cycle SHA: origin/main merge base; I did the full read at a1985d436f15 and re-checked the deltas a1985d4..13a26b4 (settings-api fix, commit 52448581) and 13a26b4..9f37570 (one test file and plan artifacts only). No source the blockers depend on changed after a1985d4.

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] Desktop packaging omits `@hyperswarm/secret-stream`, so the packaged server fails at import — `src/lib/anywhere/channel/channel-socket.ts:62`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect, in_pr_scope. D-4645-2 covers the tsdown `neverBundle` lists but says nothing about desktop packaging (a spec gap).
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `channel-socket.ts` loads the library at module top level with `_require('@hyperswarm/secret-stream')`. tsdown inlines that as `createRequire(import.meta.url)("@hyperswarm/secret-stream")` in the `dashboard-auth-*` chunk, which `server.js` imports at boot (`channel-peer.ts` → `dashboard-auth.ts`). The desktop packager (`apps/desktop/scripts/prepare-server-resources.mjs`) installs only the externals that `apps/desktop/scripts/import-closure.mjs` finds. Its regexes match `from "x"`, `import "x"`, `import("x")` and `require("x")`, and none of them matches `Require(import.meta.url)("x")`.
- Expected / observed / impact: Expected: the packaged server installs every runtime external. Observed: when I run the scanner on the built `dist/dashboard`, it reports `noise-handshake true` (found only through `_require("noise-handshake/dh")`), `@hyperswarm/secret-stream false`, `sodium-universal false` and `sodium-native false`. `noise-handshake`'s dependencies are `b4a`, `nanoassert` and `sodium-universal`, so secret-stream is not installed transitively. The generated stub `package.json` therefore lacks it. In the packaged desktop app, `server.js` throws "module not found" while importing the dashboard-auth chunk, so the dashboard never boots. The npm/`pan` install path is not affected because it installs every root dependency.
- Evidence: I ran `scanImportClosure('dist/dashboard', [server.js, deacon.js, …])` with the repo's own module on the build output. I read the inlined line `const SecretStream = createRequire(import.meta.url)("@hyperswarm/secret-stream");` in `dist/dashboard/dashboard-auth-BeQqhMkJ.js`. I read the dependency lists from `node_modules/*/package.json`. Limit: I did not run a full desktop build or launch the packaged app. No PR CI job runs desktop packaging, so CI cannot catch this.
- Fix: use one of these. (a) Import the two libraries statically (`import SecretStream from '@hyperswarm/secret-stream'` and `import Noise from 'noise-handshake'`) so the bundle emits `from "…"`. (b) Teach `import-closure.mjs` the `createRequire\([^)]*\)\(\s*["']([^"'\n]+)["']` shape. (c) Pin the four Noise packages explicitly in `prepare-server-resources.mjs`. Whichever you pick, also confirm that `sodium-native` loads under Electron, the same way the script already verifies node-pty.

### [security] A revoked `/ws/rpc` connection keeps executing RPCs until the peer answers the close frame (up to 30 s) — `src/dashboard/server/ws-rpc-auth.ts:121`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect (a regression from baseline), in_pr_scope (WI-7 / D-4645-15). D-4645-15 asked for a 4401 close frame. It did not ask to drop the handler interrupt.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: on main, `/ws/rpc` raced the RPC handler against a revocation `Deferred`, so a revoke interrupted the handler fiber at once. This PR removes that `raceFirst` (see the `ws-rpc.ts` diff). `withRpcRevocation` → `closeRpcSocketRevoked` now only calls `ws.close(4401)`. With `ws`, `close()` moves the socket to CLOSING and arms a 30 s close timer. Received messages are still emitted (`receiverOnMessage` has no state check). Effect's `fromWebSocket` removes its `message` listener only on the `close` event (`effect/dist/unstable/socket/Socket.js:367-400`).
- Expected / observed / impact: Expected: the credential stops working the moment it is revoked, as it did on main. Observed: a client that does not answer the close frame keeps a working RPC channel with the revoked credential's scopes until ws's 30 s close timeout. Device credentials carry `admin`. A stolen device is exactly the case revocation exists for. Machine credentials are not affected, because `closeChannelsForPeer` destroys their channel sockets.
- Evidence: in a scratch probe (`scratchpad/wsprobe/probe.cjs`, using the repo's `ws`), the server called `close(4401)` and the client paused its socket so it never answered. The server still received all 5 later messages in readyState 2, and the socket was still open after 3 s. The Effect side is a static trace, not a run of the full RPC stack. The new `ws-rpc-revoke.test.ts` checks only that a compliant client sees 4401.
- Fix: keep both behaviours. In the revocation callback, send `ws.close(4401, 'device revoked')` and then complete a `Deferred` that `raceFirst`s the RPC handler (the main-branch shape). The handler fiber stops processing, and the 4401 frame is already queued.

## Non-blocking Findings
- `~` [spec conflict] Commit 52448581 reverts PRD WI-15 step 2. `loadSettingsApi` reports `requireTokenMint` (the enforced value) again, not `.configured`, so that the existing D-1 test passes. The PRD chose `.configured` so that the whole-document Settings save would not write an automatic `true` back to `config.yaml`. Now any Settings save while a device, link or trusted address exists persists `require_token_mint: true`. It stays on after everything is unlinked, until the operator turns the toggle off. This is safe but sticky. The deviation is not recorded against the PRD's WI-15 test ("Settings GET reports `require_token_mint: false`"). Decide between two fixes: keep enforced reporting and skip writing the key while it is on automatically, or restore `.configured` and amend the D-1 test.
- `~` [must-not] `src/lib/settings-api.ts` grew from 1503 lines on main to 1504 at HEAD (one comment line from 52448581). Non-goal 9 says it must not grow. It stays under the 1508 allowlist cap, so lint stays green. Drop the extra comment line.
- `~` [latent, downstream] `rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest` (`dashboard-auth.ts:260`) still calls `resolveDashboardCredential(headers)` without the channel. On a plain resolve a machine credential returns `null`, so the guard demands Origin and CSRF headers that a linked machine never has, and answers 403. Stop, abort, lanes, send and the permission routes use `validateOrigin` and are not affected. `POST /api/workers`, which has an operate row, uses this guard, so a machine credential passes the gate and then gets 403 from the route. Use `resolveRequestCredential(request)` there and treat `machine` as a header-borne credential that skips the CSRF check, before #4651 forwards worker spawns.
- `~` [spec deviation] The pairing credential is consumed in `takePairingById` (preamble time), not when the handshake succeeds. `PairingSecret.onSuccess` is never set (`server.ts`). The pairing id travels in the cleartext preamble, so an on-path observer, or a failure after the preamble, burns the code. The impact is a retry with a new `pan pair` link. Either consume in `onSuccess` or update the interface comment.
- `~` `MACHINE_TOKEN_SCOPES('operator')` adds `approve`, which FR-7's list does not contain. This reconciles the PRD with PAN-4649, which moved the permission routes to `approve` after the PRD was written, and the new test pins it. Amend FR-7 to match.
- `~` The supervisor marks a link permanently `revoked` (persisted with `markLinkRevoked`) on a single refusal `01`. On the peer, refusal `01` also happens when `access-tokens.json` is temporarily unreadable, because the snapshot is cleared. A transient corrupt file on the peer therefore forces a re-link. Consider re-probing once before persisting.
- `~` Race: `applyDescriptor` persists `entry.link.routes` that it computed before an `await`. An Add route that lands in between can be overwritten.
- `?` `handleMachinesExchange` trusts the `environmentId` in the request body for the D-4645-18 replace. The holder of a pairing code can therefore revoke another environment's inbound token by claiming its id. This needs a code that the operator issued, and that code is already admin-equivalent.
- `?` `/ws/link` does not refuse Tailscale Funnel requests, unlike `authorizeDashboardUpgrade`. When Funnel is on, the pre-auth handshake surface, including the global cap of 32 pending handshakes, is reachable from the internet. Decide whether Funnel is a valid link route.
- `?` The connection dispatcher's `socket.setTimeout(10_000, () => socket.destroy())` leaves its `once('timeout')` listener in place after `setTimeout(0)`. A later Node HTTP timeout on that socket destroys it directly. Node destroys idle keep-alive sockets anyway, so I see no current impact.
- Performance (advisory): `ensureMachineKey()` reads `machine-key.json` from disk on every unauthenticated `GET /api/environment` and on every supervisor probe. The file is small and the read is async; caching it after the first read would be cheap.
- Compliance note: D-4645-13 is always on. A browser on another LAN device that uses plain `http://<lan-ip>:3011` now gets the 403 "Use HTTPS" page. `configuration/remote-access.mdx` documents this.

## Coverage

- Reviewed, channel/link core: `channel/{wire,noise,accept,open,channel-socket,channel-agent}.ts`, `channel-listener.ts`, `channel-peer.ts`, `server.ts`, `machine-key.ts`, `link-store.ts`, `routes.ts`, `endpoints.ts`, `link-actor.ts`, `link-client.ts`.
- Reviewed, routes and services: `machines.ts`, `machines-peer.ts`, `machine-link-service.ts`, `link-supervisor.ts`, `link-heartbeat.ts`, `anywhere-boot.ts`, `event-loop-monitor.ts`, `remote-request-gate.ts`, `route-scopes.ts`, `device-connections.ts`, `pairing-credentials.ts`, `routes/pairing.ts`, `plain-http-guard.ts`, `environment.ts`, `anywhere.ts`, `dashboard-session.ts`, `events.ts`, `vault.ts`, `ws-terminal.ts`, `ws-voice.ts`, `ws-autopreso.ts`, `main.ts`, `boot-gates.ts`.
- Reviewed, data: `infra.ts`, `conversation-environment.ts`, `conversations.ts` (size and insert site), `conversation-archive.ts` (moved listing), `conversation-vault-rows.ts`, `vault/browse.ts` (wired through `vault-browse-service.ts`), `remote-access/config.ts`, `anywhere-status.ts`, `settings-api.ts`.
- Reviewed, CLI and UI: `machines.ts`, `pair.ts`, `dashboard-call.ts`, `MachinesPanel.tsx`, `LinkMachineDialog.tsx`, `machinesApi.ts`, `anywhereApi.ts`, `AnywhereSection.tsx`, `Toggle.tsx`.
- Reviewed, contracts and build: `contracts/{environment,machines,index}.ts`, `package.json`, both `tsdown.config.ts` files, the desktop packager interaction (`apps/desktop/scripts/import-closure.mjs` and `prepare-server-resources.mjs`, unchanged but affected).
- Reviewed, docs: `docs.json`, `CLAUDE.md` row, `SKILLS-CONVENTION.md`, `architecture.md`, and the superseded headers on pan-2352/2356/3513. pan-2355 carries no header because it has been rebaselined on pan-2350 r5, so the header no longer applies. `ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md`, `linked-machines.mdx`, `cli/machines.mdx`, `remote-access.mdx` and `DASHBOARD-AUTH.md` were spot-checked.
- Tests: the security and channel suites listed under Verification, plus the names of the remaining new test files. Smoke: `scripts/anywhere/two-machine-smoke.mjs`; its deletions are limited to `.tmp/anywhere-[ab]`.
- Not applicable: `.pan/*` artifacts, `bun.lock`, `composer-commands.generated.ts`, `harness-branches-baseline.txt`, `frontend-test-subset.txt` (I checked that the new UI test is listed).

**Stub-UI findings:** all five are false positives. Every flagged state has a writer: the `setRoutesOpen` toggle, `setBusy` in the action handlers, `setLinking` in `handleLink`, and the `setLinkOpen` button.

**Dimensions:** correctness, security, performance and requirements/UX are all covered, with the findings above.

## Verification
- CI for 9f37570f: build, lint groups, test shards, e2e and clean-install are all **pending**, so they are unverified. The overdeck/test gate passed (typecheck and lint). The previous head failed test shard 1 on settings-api.test.ts; commit 52448581 addresses that.
- I ran `npx vitest run` on channel, channel-capture, channel-listener, machine-credential, ws-rpc-revoke, ws-rpc-auth, route-scopes-machine, machines-exchange and link-supervisor at a1985d4: 9 files and 78 tests passed. None of those sources changed after that.
- I ran the desktop externals scanner on the built `dist/dashboard`: secret-stream is missing (blocker 1).
- I ran a ws close-frame probe in the scratchpad: messages are still delivered in CLOSING state (blocker 2).
- `npm run lint:effect-diagnostics`: **unverified**. My one local attempt was killed (exit 137) before it reported, and CI lint-group (effect) is pending.
- I did not run the full test suite (per the role rules) or the desktop build.
